channel.title: Pier & Point · Arthur and Toni Rembe Rock Hall
channel.description: Changes, corrections and dated milestones for Arthur and Toni Rembe Rock Hall (Mission Bay), San Francisco. Every item names its source.

item.title: Correction · Arthur and Toni Rembe Rock Hall: Rock Hall's opening note no longer says its year is contested; the only cited source, UCSF's history page, gives 2004.
item.description: Rock Hall's opening note no longer says its year is contested; the only cited source, UCSF's history page, gives 2004. Source: https://history.library.ucsf.edu/1990.html.

item.title: Correction · Arthur and Toni Rembe Rock Hall: The record said Rock Hall was notable for early use of Japanese seismic-isolation technology. Forell/Elsesser's project page says the technology was buckling-restrained braces designed and procured with Nippon Steel, new to California practice, so the summary, facts and map notes now say that. The gross area was given as 165,000-171,643 sq ft from unnamed sources; Forell gives 165,000 and the May 2000 UC Regents item gives 170,965 gsf, so those two figures are now stated with their sources. Cesar Pelli's name now cites the Regents item, since the Forell page names Pelli Clarke Pelli Architects and Flad Architects only. The opening date read June 2004 with only a website domain as its citation; the UCSF history page supports the year only, so it now reads 2004. The Regents presentation photo no longer carries a taken date (the slide is undated) or the committee name, and the April 2005 award mention is flagged as resting on an unreadable page. The Wikimedia aerial credit names only the Commons username Firstcultural.

item.title: Added · Arthur and Toni Rembe Rock Hall: The March 2000 UC Regents item approves an $88 million project budget for the Mission Bay Developmental Biology and Genetics Building (Building 19B). It is identified as Rock Hall by matching architect, size and program to the May 2000 Regents design-approval item that recounts the budget action; neither item uses the name 'Rock Hall', so the match is inferred, not certain.

item.title: Planned · Arthur and Toni Rembe Rock Hall: UC Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings certifies a CEQA EIR addendum and approves the design of the Mission Bay Developmental Biology and Genetics Building (Building 19B) -- believed to be this building based on matching architect (Cesar Pelli and Associates with Flad Associates as executive architect), size (~171,000 gsf) and programs (human genetics, developmental neuroscience, developmental biology), though the Regents item does not use the 'Rock Hall' name; an $88,000,000 total project budget was approved in March 2000, with construction slated for 2001-2003 (May 2000)
